why: phase-488 (2026-10-21). rclcpp's thread-pool executor. DECLINED for RFC-0002's reason: an executor dispatches on ONE RTOS task with run-to-completion callbacks, and nano-ros starts no thread behind the caller's back, so a pool of workers sharing an arena is not a shape it has -- and every callback group is mutually exclusive by construction (`cpp:Node::create_callback_group`). Parallelism here is per TIER: one executor per task, declared in the system description. REFUSE-LOUD rather than absent: `rclcpp::executors::MultiThreadedExecutor` exists so that DECLARING one is a compile error carrying `NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_MULTI_THREADED_EXECUTOR`, which names `SingleThreadedExecutor` and tiers, instead of "'executors' has not been declared". Held by `ros2_refuse_multi_threaded_executor_probe.cpp`. Measured on the stock `multithreaded_executor` example: the rename to `SingleThreadedExecutor` is 1 of its 26 remaining edited lines; the rest are callback groups and pointer-shaped callbacks.
